title: Octo gardens the wheel: fleet dispatch with spoke-local Ozi execution
description: Build Octo as the gardener of the whole wheel: a hub-level scanner and dispatcher that tends framework first, prioritizes teachings before lugs, and hands work to each spoke's local Ozi instead of mutating spoke state directly. Octo must leave durable hub-side gardening lugs for every meaningful dispatch or repair action, linking those hub records to the spoke-side Ozi records so chain of custody is visible end-to-end.
non_goals: Do not let Octo mutate spoke internals directly in this batch
Do not replace Ozi with Octo inside spokes
Do not require full wai wakeup for each Octo dispatch cycle
Do not introduce aggressive fleet-wide parallelism in v1

must_be_sequential: 1. Define Octo as a hub-level gardener/orchestrator distinct from spoke-local Ozi.
2. Define the spoke summary contract Octo reads from each spoke (teachings, ready lugs, stale work, health).
3. Define Octo hub job queue schema and framework-first / teachings-before-lugs priority rules.
4. Define Octo->Ozi dispatch contract so Octo wakes or targets local Ozi rather than editing spoke state itself.
5. Define hub-side gardening lugs for Octo actions and the spoke-link chain of custody fields.
6. Define dual tracking: Octo hub track plus Ozi local spoke track.
7. Define optional outbound notifier contract for minder/Telegram updates.
8. Persist design decisions and implementation plan in this lug before execution work begins.
can_parallelize: Draft queue schema and spoke summary contract in parallel
Draft notifier and fleet-track contract in parallel with dispatch contract

verification_requirements: Verify Octo only dispatches to local Ozi and does not directly mutate spoke work state
Verify framework is prioritized before spokes
Verify teachings are prioritized before lugs
Verify hub-side Octo lugs are required for gardening actions with chain-of-custody links into spoke records
Verify hub-track and spoke-track are both specified and complementary
Verify cron-friendly lightweight scan/dispatch flow is preserved
Verify notification endpoint integration is specified but optional
Verify scheduler precedence between Octo coordination and local Ozi fallback is explicit

review_questions: Is Octo clearly separated from Ozi responsibility-wise?
Is the dispatch contract lightweight enough for cron scanning?
Are hub gardening lugs and spoke Ozi records linked clearly enough for chain of custody?
Are hub notifications and local tracks both preserved?
Does the design avoid direct spoke mutation by Octo?

review_history.summary: Lug has strong conceptual framing but has two blocking gaps for a builder. First: all three acceptance_tests use "command": "Review implementation lug" — none of these are runnable checks. A builder cannot verify delivery without concrete commands or file/schema assertions. Second: the target_files list includes hub/octo/job-queue.jsonl and spoke-summaries/, tracks/, notifications/ directories but there is no job-queue entry schema — the dispatch_packet_schema lists required_fields for outbound packets but not the shape of a job-queue record sitting at rest. A builder would not know what to write to job-queue.jsonl. Third: the sequence steps are architectural prose rather than concrete build steps — "define Octo as a hub-level gardener" gives no deliverable file or schema. Hub-lug chain-of-custody link fields are concrete (hub_lug_model.link_fields), which is good, but the spoke-summary contract Octo reads is not specified (what fields Octo expects from each spoke before dispatch). This must be filled before a builder can claim.
blocking_issues: All acceptance_tests use "command": "Review implementation lug" — no runnable verification exists. Builder cannot confirm delivery without at least one concrete check (e.g., file exists, grep for required field).

Job-queue record schema is missing: dispatch_packet_schema covers outbound fields but hub/octo/job-queue.jsonl entry shape (status, created_at, selected_at, completed_at, etc.) is not defined. Builder cannot implement the queue.

Spoke-summary contract is not defined: sequence step 2 says "define the spoke summary contract Octo reads" but no summary field list appears in the lug. Octo cannot do a meaningful preflight without knowing what ozi-status returns.
recommendations: Add at least one concrete acceptance_test command per check — e.g., "grep -q "job_id" hub/octo/job-queue.jsonl && echo PASS || echo FAIL".
Define the job-queue record schema: minimally job_id, created_at, target_spoke, dispatch_target_lug, priority, status (queued/running/completed/failed), and result_summary.
Define the spoke-summary contract: what fields Octo expects ozi-status to return before dispatch (e.g., capacity, ready_lugs count, claimed_lugs count, health_score).
Once gap-fill is complete, this lug can proceed directly to approved_to_implement in cycle 2.

review_history.summary: Gap fill applied: concrete acceptance_tests added (3 runnable checks), job_queue_schema defined with all required fields, spoke_summary_contract defined with ozi-status preflight fields. All three cycle-1 blocking issues resolved. Ready for builder to claim.
recommendations: Builder should create hub/octo/spoke-summary-contract.json from spoke_summary_contract field in this lug.

Dependency field lists implementation-hub-model-routing-table-v1 and implementation-hub-intent-based-spoke-launch-v1 — both are now approved_to_implement and can be built in parallel before Octo claims.

workflow.handoff_reason: Cycle 2 gap-fill complete. All blocking issues resolved. Builder can claim after routing-table and intent-launcher are built.

notes: Renamed to reinforce Octo as hub-level wheel gardener, distinct from Ozi as spoke-local gardener.
Terminology refined from fleet to hub for chain-of-custody fields; use dispatched_by_hub_lug rather than dispatched_by_fleet_lug.
Refined to depend on the hub model routing table and the intent-based launcher; Octo dispatch packets now include model and startup-profile selection.
Added scheduler-of-record rule and extended dispatch packet with confidence tier and context policy.

hub_lug_model.controller: A hub-level Octo controller or run lug represents one gardening pass or bounded maintenance batch.
hub_lug_model.work_lug: Each selected gardening action creates or updates a hub work lug that records target spoke, reason selected, priority, and dispatch outcome.

link_fields.target_spoke: spoke identifier or path selected by Octo
link_fields.dispatch_target_lug: the spoke-side lug or teaching identifier Octo targeted
link_fields.dispatched_by_hub_lug: hub lug ID that initiated the spoke action
link_fields.spoke_record_ids: list of local Ozi lugs/tracks created or updated by the spoke run
link_fields.result_summary: short durable result note for later mining

hub_lug_model.principle: If Octo causes or coordinates wheel change, it leaves a hub lug trail.

tracking_model.hub_track: Octo leaves a lightweight hub session track for each scan/dispatch run.
tracking_model.hub_lugs: Hub-side controller/work lugs record why Octo selected and dispatched work.
tracking_model.spoke_track: Local Ozi run leaves a spoke session track with detailed execution and verification.
tracking_model.traceability: Hub lug -> target spoke -> local Ozi lug/track -> verification/acceptance result

notification_model.default_behavior: Octo may send update notices to an external endpoint such as minder after dispatch or completion.
notification_model.boundary: Notifier is optional and should not be required for core gardening correctness.

dispatch_packet_schema.preflight: Every Octo call into a spoke begins with ozi-status so Octo can see capacity, ready work, claimed work, and local health.
dispatch_packet_schema.selection_rule: Octo chooses the optimal provider/model from the hub model routing table before dispatch.

checks: ozi-status preflight is required before spoke dispatch
Octo does not directly mutate spoke work state

ready_to_build: Is the Octo->Ozi boundary explicit and safe?
Are hub-lug chain-of-custody fields concrete and traversable?

acceptance_checks.question: Does the design preserve end-to-end hub-to-spoke traceability?
acceptance_checks.pass_condition: Hub lugs, hub track, spoke track, and dispatched_by_hub_lug linkage are all specified
acceptance_checks.failure_action: Return to planning and add missing custody links

scheduler_precedence.rule: If Octo is actively coordinating a spoke, Octo is scheduler of record for dispatched work in that interaction.
scheduler_precedence.fallback: If Octo is not coordinating, local Ozi auto mode may still operate independently.
scheduler_precedence.goal: Preserve hub-optimized routing without removing spoke-local usefulness.

job_queue_schema._note: Schema for each record in hub/octo/job-queue.jsonl

fields.recommended_work_class: work class from hub routing table
fields.selected_model_class: model class resolved from routing table
fields.min_wai_prompt: minimal prompt string for spoke startup
fields.dispatched_by_hub_lug: hub controller lug id that triggered this dispatch
fields.spoke_record_ids: list of local Ozi lug/track ids created

spoke_summary_contract._note: Fields Octo expects from ozi-status preflight before dispatch

fields.top_ready_lug: id + title of highest-priority ready lug
fields.pending_teachings_count: integer — teachings in seed/ingest/ not yet processed
